assets.request: Paint Unit One, an inexpensive lakeside motel room, seen from the doorway. A neatly pulled thin bedspread, mismatched bedside table, worn chair, a plain key on the table, coat hook, old baseboard heater under a window. Beyond the window blue lake darkness and a little wharf light. Amber bedside lamp, rubbed veneer and clean but aging surfaces. No people, no mirrors, no protagonist reflection. Modest shelter someone has made ready, rather than a grand hotel or ruin.

assets.request: Paint the old ferry wharf and compressor shed. View from inside the open weathered timber machinery shed, compressor pressure gauge and coiled hose at one edge; through the open doorway wet plank walkway extends over black lake water toward a small brass horn facing the lake. Frost and orchard hillside across the bay, one amber work light. The shed is maintained by someone who knows machinery, with practical tools arranged within reach. No people. Keep the walkway and horn readable together. No ocean, no large ship, no oversized foghorn tower.

assets.request: Paint the town’s small working clinic: one examination room with a paper-covered couch, desk with a closed notebook and plain mug, handwashing sink and a worn rolling stool. Cold overcast daylight from a high window meets a small warm desk lamp; restrained fluorescent ceiling light. Everyday, competent and slightly cramped rather than sinister. Lake-grey walls, pale green upholstery, scuffed cream linoleum. A coat on a hook suggests someone has just stepped out. No people, no readable patient details, no gore, no modern hospital machinery.

assets.request: Paint Sam’s boathouse workshop, distinct from the compressor wharf. View past an old timber workbench with a small wooden boat part being sanded, clamps, curled shavings, a mug and a guitar leaning safely on the wall. A partly open wide door looks onto dark lake water with rope and a little dinghy outside. Bare bulb and amber work lamp, blue afternoon reflected from water, untidy but deliberate human occupation. Leave floor room for two people to work. No people, no instruments with surreal strings, no ornate or abandoned ruin.

assets.request: Paint the modest community hall on a quiet afternoon before anyone arrives: scuffed wooden floor, folded trestle tables along one wall, stackable chairs, upright piano and plain noticeboard, a serving hatch toward a tiny kitchen. Tall windows show bare orchard branches against cold grey-blue daylight. Amber light pools above the serving hatch. A clean cloth and kettle ready for work. Low ordinary ceiling and recognizable small-town proportions, no ballroom or church altar. No people. The room should be able to host a memorial potluck later.

assets.request: Paint the little roadside bus shelter at Lorn Bay’s highway pull-in. Weathered timber and rain-streaked glass, a wooden bench, timetable case with indistinct marks, damp asphalt and a narrow road bend. Beyond it rows of leafless orchard trees descend toward the cold inland lake and rounded hills. Pale late-autumn afternoon, one warm shelter lamp. The shelter and empty road should be central, waiting rather than desolate. No bus and no people yet, no readable lettering, no ocean, no city buildings.
